# SBoM v0.10.0 - Table of Contents

Mix task to generate a Software Bill-of-Materials (SBoM) in CycloneDX format

## Modules

- [SBoM](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.md): <!--
  SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
  SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2019 Bram Verburg
  SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025 Erlang Ecosystem Foundation
-->
- [SBoM.CycloneDX](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.md): SBoM CycloneDX encoding and decoding.
- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Aggregate](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Aggregate.md): CycloneDX Aggregate model.
- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.AttachedText](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.AttachedText.md): Specifies attributes of the text

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Bom](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Bom.md): CycloneDX Bom model.
- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Classification](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Classification.md): CycloneDX Classification model.
- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Commit](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Commit.md): CycloneDX Commit model.

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.DataClassification](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.DataClassification.md): Specifies the data classification.

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.DataFlow](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.DataFlow.md): Specifies the flow direction of the data. Valid values are: inbound, outbound, bi-directional, and unknown. Direction is relative to the service. Inbound flow states that data enters the service. Outbound flow states that data leaves the service. Bi-directional states that data flows both ways, and unknown states that the direction is not known.

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Pedigree](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V13.Pedigree.md): Component pedigree is a way to document complex supply chain scenarios where components are created, distributed, modified, redistributed, combined with other components, etc. Pedigree supports viewing this complex chain from the beginning, the end, or anywhere in the middle. It also provides a way to document variants where the exact relation may not be known.

Valid values are: inbound, outbound, bi-directional, and unknown. Direction is relative to the service. Inbound flow states that data enters the service. Outbound flow states that data leaves the service. Bi-directional states that data flows both ways, and unknown states that the direction is not known.

Components or services that do not have their own dependencies must be declared as empty elements within the graph. Components or services that are not represented in the dependency graph may have unknown dependencies. It is recommended that implementations assume this to be opaque and not an indicator of an object being dependency-free. It is recommended to leverage compositions to indicate unknown dependency graphs.

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V16.LicenseAcknowledgementEnumeration](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V16.LicenseAcknowledgementEnumeration.md): Declared licenses and concluded licenses represent two different stages in the licensing process within software development. Declared licenses refer to the initial intention of the software authors regarding the licensing terms under which their code is released. On the other hand, concluded licenses are the result of a comprehensive analysis of the project's codebase to identify and confirm the actual licenses of the components used, which may differ from the initially declared licenses. While declared licenses provide an upfront indication of the licensing intentions, concluded licenses offer a more thorough understanding of the actual licensing within a project, facilitating proper compliance and risk management. Observed licenses are defined in `@.evidence.licenses`. Observed licenses form the evidence necessary to substantiate a concluded license.

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.DataFlow](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.DataFlow.md): Specifies the data flow.

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.DataFlowDirection](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.DataFlowDirection.md): Specifies the flow direction of the data. Valid values are: inbound, outbound, bi-directional, and unknown. Direction is relative to the service. Inbound flow states that data enters the service. Outbound flow states that data leaves the service. Bi-directional states that data flows both ways, and unknown states that the direction is not known.
buf:lint:ignore ENUM_VALUE_PREFIX -- Enum value names should be prefixed with "DATA_FLOW_DIRECTION_"

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.LicenseAcknowledgementEnumeration](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.LicenseAcknowledgementEnumeration.md): Declared licenses and concluded licenses represent two different stages in the licensing process within software development. Declared licenses refer to the initial intention of the software authors regarding the licensing terms under which their code is released. On the other hand, concluded licenses are the result of a comprehensive analysis of the project's codebase to identify and confirm the actual licenses of the components used, which may differ from the initially declared licenses. While declared licenses provide an upfront indication of the licensing intentions, concluded licenses offer a more thorough understanding of the actual licensing within a project, facilitating proper compliance and risk management. Observed licenses are defined in `@.evidence.licenses`. Observed licenses form the evidence necessary to substantiate a concluded license.

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.LicenseChoice](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.LicenseChoice.md): CycloneDX LicenseChoice model.

It must be a valid SPDX license expression, along with additional properties such as license acknowledgment.

- [SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.LicenseExpressionDetailed.ExpressionDetails](https://sbom.hexdocs.pm/SBoM.CycloneDX.V17.LicenseExpressionDetailed.ExpressionDetails.md): This document specifies the details and attributes related to a software license identifier. An SPDX expression may be a compound of license identifiers.
The `license_identifier` field serves as the key that identifies each record. Note that this key is not required to be unique, as the same license identifier could apply to multiple, different but similar license details, texts, etc.

These patents are filed in multiple jurisdictions to protect the invention across different regions or countries. A patent family typically includes patents that share a common priority date, originating from the same initial application, and may vary slightly in scope or claims to comply with regional legal frameworks.
